figures.caption: Figure 1. Comparison between conventional and interpretable ML frameworks for battery prognosis. (a) Conventional ML workﬂow: Battery datasets undergo feature engineering and are fed into black-box models to predict battery targets, such as SOH, RUL and SOC. The model outputs are delivered directly to users or domain experts, but they are not interpretable. (b) Interpretable ML framework: Based on the conventional ML workﬂow, this frame- work incorporates physical knowledge or post-hoc explainable tools to enhance model transparency. This interpretability enables a better understanding of the model’s behavior, supports its validation and optimization, and facilitates the extraction of knowledge for battery material design and system-level improvement.
